questions.question: Which Article states that it shall be the duty of every citizen of India to abide by the constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Article 51A (a)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 51A (a)** is part of the **Fundamental Duties** outlined in the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• It specifies that it is the **duty of every citizen of India** to **abide by the Constitution**, respect its **ideals and institutions**, and honor the **National Flag** and the **National Anthem**.
 
• The concept of Fundamental Duties was introduced by the **42nd Amendment Act of 1976**, based on the recommendations of the **Swaran Singh Committee**.
 
• Fundamental Duties are inspired by the Constitution of the former **USSR** (now Russia) and aim to emphasize the importance of citizens' responsibilities toward the nation.
 
• Currently, there are **11 Fundamental Duties** enshrined in **Part IVA** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These duties serve as a reminder to citizens to uphold the **spirit of patriotism** and promote harmony and respect for constitutional values.
 
• Although Fundamental Duties are not legally enforceable, they provide a moral and ethical framework for citizens to follow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 52**__

 __
 
• **Article 52** of the Indian Constitution states that there shall be a **President of India**.
 
• The President is the **head of the State** and the **Executive**, and serves as the **supreme commander of the armed forces**.
 
• The President is elected by an **electoral college** comprising elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the Legislative Assemblies of the states and Union territories.
 
 
 
• **Article 14**__
 __
 
• **Article 14** guarantees the **Right to Equality** to all citizens of India.
 
• It ensures **equality before the law** and equal protection of laws within the territory of India.
 
• This article prohibits any form of **discrimination** and promotes equal treatment in similar circumstances.
 
 
 
• **Article 54 (b)**__
 
 
• **Article 54** deals with the **election of the President** of India.
 
• It specifies that the President shall be elected by an **electoral college** consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the states.
 
• The provision under **Article 54 (b)** does not directly relate to the duties of citizens but rather to the electoral process for the President.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about phylum Arthropoda are correct?

A. Animals of Arthropoda have joint appendages.

B. They have compounds eyes.

C. These make up the majority of all animals on earth.

D. The mode of reproduction in all Arthropods is vegetative.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Only A, B and C**

__**Concept:**__

**Characteristics of Arthropoda:**

__
 
• This is the largest phylum of Animalia which includes insects. Over two-thirds of all named species on earth are arthropods.
 
• They have organ-system level of organisation.
 
• They are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic, segmented and coelomate animals.
 
• The body of arthropods is covered by chitinous exoskeleton.
 
• The body consists of head, thorax and abdomen.
 
• They have jointed appendages (arthros-joint, poda-appendages).
 
• Respiratory organs are gills, book gills, book lungs or tracheal system. The circulatory system is of open type.
 
• Sensory organs like antennae, eyes (compound and simple), statocysts or balancing organs are present.
 
• Excretion takes place through malpighian tubules.
 
• They are mostly dioecious. Fertilisation is usually internal. They are mostly oviparous.
 
• Development may be direct or indirect.
 
• Examples: Economically important insects – Apis (Honey bee), Bombyx (Silkworm), Laccifer (Lac insect), Anopheles, Culex and Aedes (Mosquitoes) Locusta (Locust), Living fossil – Limulus (King crab).

**Explanation:**__

**A. Animals of the Arthropoda have joint appendages. (Correct)**

 
• The characteristic features of arthropods are their jointed appendages. 

**B. They have compound eyes. (Correct)**

 
• Arthropods often possess compound eyes, which are made up of multiple individual units called ommatidia. Each ommatidium functions as a separate visual receptor, enabling arthropods to have a broad field of vision and to detect movement efficiently. This feature is particularly important for their survival.

**C. These make up the majority of all animals on earth. (Correct)**

 
• This is the largest phylum of Animalia which includes insects. Over two-thirds of all named species on earth are arthropods

**D. The mode of reproduction in all Arthropods is vegetative. (Incorrect)**

 
• The statement is incorrect because arthropods do not reproduce vegetatively.
 
• Reproduction in arthropods is primarily sexual, involving the fusion of male and female gametes. Many arthropods engage in complex mating behaviors and lay eggs, although some species may give birth to live young.

questions.question: The construction of Humayun's tomb was completed by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Biga Begum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The construction of **Humayun's Tomb** was commissioned by his widow, **Biga Begum**, also known as **Haji Begum**.
 
• It was built in memory of the Mughal Emperor **Humayun** and is considered the first significant example of **Mughal architecture** in India.
 
• The tomb was designed by the Persian architect **Mirak Mirza Ghiyas**, reflecting the **Persian style of architecture** with Indian influences.
 
• The construction was completed in the year **1571**, about 15 years after Humayun's death in **1556**.
 
• It is located in **Delhi, India**, and is a UNESCO **World Heritage Site**.
 
• The complex is known for its **charbagh (four-part) garden layout**, which became a hallmark of Mughal gardens.
 
• **Red sandstone and white marble** were extensively used in its construction, showcasing the grandeur of the Mughal era.
 
• The structure served as inspiration for later Mughal monuments, including the **Taj Mahal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Zeenat Mahal**__

 __
 
• **Zeenat Mahal** was the wife of the last Mughal Emperor **Bahadur Shah Zafar**.
 
• She was known for her influence in the Mughal court during the declining years of the empire.
 
• She had no connection with the construction of **Humayun's Tomb**.
 
 
 
• **Mah Chuchak Begum**__
 __
 
• **Mah Chuchak Begum** was a wife of **Humayun** and played a political role during the Mughal reign.
 
• She was known for her governance in **Kabul** after Humayun's death.
 
• However, she was not involved in the construction of **Humayun's Tomb**.
 
 
 
• **Rahmat Banu Begum**__
 
 
• **Rahmat Banu Begum** was the daughter of **Humayun**.
 
• There is no historical evidence of her involvement in the construction of the tomb.

questions.question: The Patli Dun is associated with which physiographic division of India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**The Himalayan Mountains**__.

• The term **Patli Dun** is used to describe a type of valley situated in the **Himalayan Mountains**.
 
• It is one of the several **dun valleys** found in the Himalayan foothills. **Duns** are longitudinal valleys formed between the Lesser Himalayas and the Shivalik hills.
 
• The word "**Dun**" originates from a local dialect and refers to the flat-bottomed valleys that are often fertile and suitable for agriculture.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements in the context of the Mughal Rule.

1. The Mansabdari System was introduced by Akbar in 1571.

2. The Second Battle of Panipat was fought in 1556.

3. Maharana Pratap Singh of Mewar was a contemporary of Babur.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Both 1 and 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mansabdari System** was introduced by **Akbar** in **1571**. It was a unique administrative system for grading officials and assigning them ranks (mansabs) based on their performance and responsibilities. This system helped in centralizing the administration and maintaining a strong military.
 
• The **Second Battle of Panipat** was fought in **1556** between the forces of the Mughal emperor Akbar, led by Bairam Khan, and the local king Hemu. This battle marked the consolidation of Mughal power in India under Akbar's rule.
 
• **Maharana Pratap Singh** of Mewar was not a contemporary of Babur but of Akbar. Babur ruled during the early 16th century, while Maharana Pratap was a 16th-century ruler who fiercely resisted Akbar's expansionist policies.
 
• The Mansabdari system and the Second Battle of Panipat are crucial milestones in Indian history as they laid the foundation for Akbar's administrative and military success.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mansabdari System**__

 __
 
• The Mansabdari system was based on the numerical rank assigned to officers, which determined their status and salary.
 
• Ranks were divided into **Zat** (personal rank) and **Sawar** (number of cavalry maintained).
 
• This system was crucial in organizing the Mughal military and administration effectively.
 
• It ensured loyalty among the officers and allowed Akbar to maintain a strong and centralized empire.
 
 
 
• **Second Battle of Panipat**__
 __
 
• This battle was significant in establishing Mughal dominance in northern India.
 
• **Hemu**, the local king, was defeated by Bairam Khan, Akbar's regent, despite putting up a strong resistance.
 
• The victory solidified Akbar's position as the ruler and marked the beginning of the Mughal Empire's golden era.
 
 
 
• **Maharana Pratap Singh**__
 
 
• Maharana Pratap was a ruler of **Mewar**, and he is remembered for his bravery and resistance against Akbar's invasions.
 
• He fought the famous **Battle of Haldighati** against Akbar's forces led by Man Singh in 1576.
 
• Maharana Pratap is considered a symbol of Rajput pride and independence.

questions.question: Who built Sudarshan lake in Junagarh?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Pushyagupta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sudarshan Lake**, located in **Junagarh**, was originally constructed by **Pushyagupta**, who served as the **governor under Chandragupta Maurya**.
 
• Pushyagupta played a significant role in the **hydraulic engineering** of the Mauryan era by undertaking this project.
 
• The lake was primarily built to support **irrigation, water conservation, and agriculture** in the region.
 
• It was later repaired and improved by rulers like **Skandagupta** and other successors.
 
• The construction of the lake is a testimony to the **advanced water management systems** of ancient India.
 
• The Sudarshan Lake has been mentioned in historical texts, including the **Junagarh Rock Inscription**, which credits Pushyagupta for its creation.
 
• This lake highlights the importance placed on sustainable water usage and infrastructure by the rulers of the **Mauryan dynasty**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Skandagupta**__

 __
 
• **Skandagupta** was a ruler of the **Gupta Empire**, known for his military accomplishments, including repelling the **Huna invasions**.
 
• Although he did not construct the Sudarshan Lake, he is credited with repairing it, as mentioned in the **Junagarh Rock Inscription**.
 
• Skandagupta’s reign was marked by economic challenges and the need to maintain the empire’s infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Chandragupta**__
 __
 
• **Chandragupta** refers to **Chandragupta Maurya**, the founder of the **Mauryan Empire**.
 
• He was the ruler under whose governance **Pushyagupta** served as a governor and built the Sudarshan Lake.
 
• Chandragupta is known for unifying the Indian subcontinent and establishing a strong administrative framework.
 
 
 
• **Bhanugupta**__
 
 
• **Bhanugupta** was a lesser-known ruler of the **Gupta dynasty**.
 
• He is primarily mentioned in inscriptions for his military campaigns, and there is no direct connection to the construction or maintenance of the Sudarshan Lake.

questions.question: Which of the following dance categories is NOT considered for an award of the Sangeet Natak Akademi?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Vilasini Natyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vilasini Natyam** is a classical Indian dance form that originated in the temples of **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• It was traditionally performed by **female temple dancers**, known as **Devadasis**, as part of religious rituals and ceremonies.
 
• This dance form is not widely practiced today and has not yet been formally recognized by the **Sangeet Natak Akademi** for an award, unlike other established classical dance forms of India.
 
• Vilasini Natyam involves intricate **footwork, hand gestures (mudras), and facial expressions (abhinaya)** to narrate stories and spiritual themes.
 
• The revival of Vilasini Natyam has been spearheaded by a few dedicated dancers and researchers, but its limited popularity has kept it outside the mainstream recognition framework.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Manipuri**__

 __
 
• **Manipuri** is one of the **eight recognized classical dance forms** of India.
 
• It originates from the northeastern state of **Manipur** and is deeply rooted in the state’s culture and traditions.
 
• Manipuri dance is characterized by its soft, graceful, and fluid movements, often associated with **Vaishnavism** and the **Raslila of Radha and Krishna**.
 
• This dance form has received recognition and awards from the **Sangeet Natak Akademi**.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi**__
 __
 
• **Kuchipudi** is another **classical dance form of India**, originating from **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• It combines **dance, music, and acting**, making it a highly expressive art form.
 
• Kuchipudi performances often narrate stories from **Hindu scriptures**, such as the **Ramayana and Mahabharata**.
 
• This dance form is recognized by the **Sangeet Natak Akademi** for awards.
 
 
 
• **Kathak**__
 
 
• **Kathak** is a classical dance form of India that has its roots in **North India**.
 
• The word "Kathak" is derived from "Katha," meaning **story**; hence, it is known as the **storytelling dance**.
 
• Kathak performances are characterized by **intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures.**
 
• This dance form is well-recognized by the **Sangeet Natak Akademi** and has received significant recognition and awards.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the notochord in chordates?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Support**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **notochord** is a flexible, rod-shaped structure that provides **support** to the body of chordates, especially during their embryonic stage.
 
• It forms the primary axis of the body and acts as a **scaffold** for the development of the vertebral column in vertebrates.
 
• The notochord is located between the digestive tube and the nerve cord and is composed of **cells derived from the mesoderm**.
 
• In most vertebrates, the notochord is replaced by the vertebral column during development, but it still plays a crucial role in **body structure and organization** during early embryogenesis.
 
• The presence of a notochord is one of the primary characteristics of the **phylum Chordata**, which includes all vertebrates, cephalochordates, and urochordates.
 
• In species like **amphioxus (lancelets)**, the notochord persists throughout life, providing continuous support and structural integrity.
 
• The notochord is also significant for inducing the development of the **neural tube**, which later forms the central nervous system, including the brain and spinal cord.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Locomotion**__

 __
 
• While the notochord provides structural **support**, it does not directly aid in **locomotion**. Instead, locomotion in chordates is facilitated by structures like **muscles and fins** or limbs.
 
• In some aquatic chordates, the notochord works in conjunction with muscles to allow a wave-like motion for **propulsion**.
 
 
 
• **Digestion**__
 __
 
• The notochord is not involved in the process of **digestion**. Digestion is carried out by the **digestive system**, which includes organs like the stomach, intestine, and associated glands.
 
• The digestive tube in chordates lies **below the notochord**.
 
 
 
• **Respiration**__
 
 
• Respiration in chordates is facilitated by specialized structures like **gills, lungs, or skin**, depending on the species and their habitat.
 
• The notochord does not play a role in **gas exchange** or respiration.

questions.question: Manipuri Raas Leela, a renowned form of classical dance, was created by:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Maharaja Bhagyachandra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Manipuri Raas Leela** is a highly revered classical dance form of **Manipur**, an Indian state in the northeastern region of the country.
 
• This dance form is deeply rooted in **Vaishnavism**, a tradition of devotion to **Lord Krishna**.
 
• **Maharaja Bhagyachandra**, a ruler of Manipur in the 18th century, is credited with conceptualizing and establishing the **Manipuri Raas Leela**.
 
• He was a devout follower of **Vaishnavism**, and under his reign, Manipuri Raas Leela was developed as a form of **spiritual expression** and to propagate the values of devotion and love for **Lord Krishna and Radha**.
 
• The dance combines **graceful movements, intricate footwork, and emotive expressions** to portray episodes from the life of **Lord Krishna**, particularly his love for **Radha**.
 
• Manipuri Raas Leela is performed during auspicious occasions such as **Janmashtami** and other festivals related to Lord Krishna.
 
• The costumes and music used in the dance reflect the **traditional culture of Manipur**. The female performers wear the iconic **Potloi** (a cylindrical skirt) while narrating the divine love story of Radha and Krishna.
 
• This dance form is characterized by its unique style of gentle and flowing movements, setting it apart from other Indian classical dance forms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Birju Maharaj**__

 __
 
• **Birju Maharaj** was a legendary exponent of **Kathak**, another classical Indian dance form.
 
• He was born in **Lucknow** and belonged to the **Kalka-Bindadin Gharana** of Kathak.
 
• He is known for his contribution to popularizing Kathak both in India and globally, but he is not associated with the creation of **Manipuri Raas Leela**.
 
 
 
• **Siddhendra Yogi**__
 __
 
• **Siddhendra Yogi** is considered to be the founder of the **Kuchipudi** dance form, which originated in **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• He played a crucial role in structuring Kuchipudi as a classical dance form with a strong connection to religious and mythological themes.
 
 
 
• **Sage Bharata**__
 
 
• **Sage Bharata** is traditionally known as the author of the **Natyashastra**, an ancient Indian treatise on performing arts, including dance, drama, and music.
 
• The Natyashastra provides the foundational principles for various Indian classical dance forms but does not directly involve the creation of **Manipuri Raas Leela**.

questions.question: Select the imbalanced chemical equation from the following.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **imbalanced chemical equation** occurs when the number of atoms for each element is not the same on both sides of the equation, violating the **Law of Conservation of Mass**.
 
• In Option 2, the chemical equation given is: **6 HClO4 + P4O10 → 4 H3PO4 + 6 Cl2O7**.
 
• On analyzing this equation:
 
 
• The total number of **oxygen atoms** on the left side is 34 (24 from HClO4 and 10 from P4O10), whereas on the right side, the total is 38 (16 from H3PO4 and 22 from Cl2O7). This imbalance clearly shows that the equation is not balanced.
 
• The number of **phosphorus atoms** is balanced (4 on both sides).
 
• The number of **hydrogen atoms** is also balanced (6 in left & 12 in right).
 
• However, the imbalance in oxygen atoms makes this an incorrect or imbalanced chemical equation.
 
 
 
• Balancing chemical equations is a crucial step in ensuring that the reaction adheres to the fundamental principles of chemistry.
 
• Option 2 is thus the correct choice, as it does not satisfy the requirements of a balanced chemical equation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 1**__

 __
 
• The equation given is **10 KClO3 + 3 P4 → 3 P4O10 + 10 KCl**.
 
• On analyzing, the number of **atoms of potassium (K), chlorine (Cl), oxygen (O), and phosphorus (P)** is equal on both sides. Hence, this equation is balanced.
 
 
 
• **Option 3**__
 __
 
• The equation given is **3 CaCl2 + 2 Na3PO4 → Ca3(PO4)2 + 6 NaCl**.
 
• On analyzing, the number of **atoms of calcium (Ca), chlorine (Cl), sodium (Na), phosphorus (P), and oxygen (O)** is balanced on both sides. Hence, this equation is correct.
 
 
 
• **Option 4**__
 
 
• The equation given is **3 Hg(OH)2 + 2 H3PO4 → Hg3(PO4)2 + 6 H2O**.
 
• On analyzing, the number of **atoms of mercury (Hg), oxygen (O), hydrogen (H), and phosphorus (P)** is equal on both sides. Hence, this equation is balanced.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about Micro Finance institutions?

options.text: Type of banking service provided to employed
Service provided to High income people only
Majority of microfinancing operations occur in developing countries

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Majority of microfinancing operations occur in developing countries**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Microfinance institutions (MFIs)** primarily target individuals in **developing countries**, where access to traditional banking services is limited.
 
• The purpose of microfinance is to provide **small-scale financial services**, such as loans, savings, insurance, and remittances, to **low-income and underserved populations**.
 
• It helps promote **financial inclusion**, empowering people to start or expand small businesses, improve their living conditions, and escape poverty.
 
• Microfinance is particularly impactful in countries across **Asia, Africa, and Latin America**, where poverty levels are higher and banking services are less accessible.
 
• Famous examples of MFIs include **Grameen Bank** in Bangladesh and **SKS Microfinance** in India.
 
• MFIs often focus on lending to **women entrepreneurs**, as they are seen as crucial contributors to household and community development.
 
• These institutions typically provide **small loans** (known as microloans) and do not offer large-scale or jumbo loans.
 
• The concept of microfinance gained global recognition after **Muhammad Yunus**, the founder of Grameen Bank, won the **Nobel Peace Prize** in **2006** for his efforts in poverty alleviation through microcredit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Type of banking service provided to employed**__

 __
 
• This option is incorrect because microfinance is not limited to employed individuals; its primary focus is on **low-income and underserved populations**, many of whom may be unemployed or self-employed.
 
• Microfinance provides financial services to individuals who lack access to **formal banking systems**.
 
 
 
• **Service provided to high-income people only**__
 __
 
• This is incorrect because microfinance is designed to serve **low-income groups**, particularly those who are excluded from traditional financial institutions.
 
• High-income individuals generally have access to **mainstream banking services** and do not require microfinance.
 
 
 
• **Can provide jumbo loan**__
 
 
• Microfinance institutions do not offer **jumbo loans**; they specialize in providing **small loans** tailored to the needs of low-income individuals.
 
• The loan sizes in microfinance are typically small to ensure affordability and repayment feasibility for borrowers.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the appointment and duties of the Attorney-General of India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Article 76**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 76** of the Indian Constitution specifically deals with the **appointment, duties, and functions** of the **Attorney-General of India**.
 
• The Attorney-General of India is the **highest law officer** in the country.
 
• The Attorney-General is appointed by the **President of India**, and their qualifications must be the same as those required for appointment as a **Judge of the Supreme Court**.
 
• The primary role of the Attorney-General is to provide legal advice to the **Government of India** and represent the government in cases of significance.
 
• The Attorney-General has the right to participate in proceedings of both the **Houses of Parliament** (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha), though they do not have the right to vote.
 
• As per **Article 76**, the Attorney-General holds office during the pleasure of the President, meaning their tenure is not fixed.
 
• The Attorney-General is also responsible for performing duties as assigned by the President under **Article 76(2)**.
 
• Although the Attorney-General is the government's legal advisor, they cannot appear against the government in any legal case.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 74**__

 __
 
• **Article 74** of the Indian Constitution pertains to the **Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister**, which aids and advises the President in the exercise of their functions.
 
• It establishes the role of the **Prime Minister** and specifies that the President must act according to the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
 
 
• **Article 80**__
 __
 
• **Article 80** deals with the composition of the **Rajya Sabha**, the upper house of the Parliament of India.
 
• It specifies the number of members, their selection method, and the representation of states and union territories.
 
 
 
• **Article 81**__
 
 
• **Article 81** of the Constitution defines the composition of the **Lok Sabha**, the lower house of Parliament.
 
• It specifies the maximum number of members and the manner in which they are elected, including representation of states and union territories.

questions.question: Which of following organisations sought to revive Vedic learning and combine it with modern education in the sciences?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Arya Samaj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Arya Samaj** was a Hindu reform movement founded by **Swami Dayananda Saraswati** in **1875**.
 
• Its primary aim was to revive the **Vedic traditions** and promote the teachings of the **Vedas** as the ultimate authority in all spheres of life.
 
• The organization sought to integrate **ancient Vedic knowledge** with **modern education in the sciences** to ensure the progress of society.
 
• The Arya Samaj emphasized the importance of **education** and established several **schools and colleges** such as the **Dayanand Anglo-Vedic (DAV) institutions** to impart a blend of Vedic and modern knowledge.
 
• The movement opposed **idolatry, superstitions, and caste-based discrimination**, advocating for social reforms such as **women’s education, widow remarriage, and the abolition of child marriage.**
 
• It also promoted the concept of **Swadeshi** (self-reliance) and contributed to the **Indian independence movement.**
 
• The Arya Samaj’s teachings are rooted in the principles of **truth, universal brotherhood, and the upliftment of society.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Satyashodhak Samaj**__

 __
 
• The **Satyashodhak Samaj** was founded by **Jyotirao Phule** in **1873** in Maharashtra.
 
• It aimed to fight against **social injustice** and the domination of the **Brahminical caste system.**
 
• The organization worked for the **upliftment of oppressed classes**, including the **Dalits** and **women.**
 
• It did not focus on integrating Vedic learning with modern education but rather on creating awareness about **equality and social reforms.**
 
 
 
• **Brahmo Samaj**__
 __
 
• The **Brahmo Samaj** was founded by **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** in **1828**.
 
• This movement aimed at **monotheism** and opposed **ritualism, idol worship, and caste discrimination.**
 
• It focused on **social and religious reforms**, such as the abolition of **Sati** and the promotion of **women's rights**, rather than the revival of Vedic learning.
 
 
 
• **Prarthana Samaj**__
 
 
• The **Prarthana Samaj** was established in **1867** in Bombay by **Atmaram Pandurang** and later supported by **M.G. Ranade**.
 
• It was a reformist movement emphasizing **monotheism** and opposing **superstitions and caste discrimination.**
 
• Unlike the Arya Samaj, it did not focus on reviving Vedic learning but concentrated on **ethical living and social reforms** such as **widow remarriage** and **women's education.**

questions.question: In which state is the 'slash and burn' agriculture known as 'Dahiya'?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the state of **Madhya Pradesh**, the practice of **'slash and burn' agriculture** is locally referred to as **'Dahiya'**.
 
• This method involves the cutting and burning of vegetation in forests or woodlands to create fields for cultivation.
 
• It is primarily used by tribal communities in **Madhya Pradesh** and other regions to temporarily enrich the soil with nutrients from the ash.
 
• Such methods are often practiced in areas with a lack of modern agricultural facilities and are considered a form of shifting cultivation.
 
• While useful in the short term, **'slash and burn'** agriculture can have long-term adverse effects on the environment, including **deforestation and soil degradation**.
 
• In India, this practice is known by different names in different regions, such as **'Jhum' in the northeastern states**, but it is specifically referred to as **'Dahiya'** in Madhya Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Himachal Pradesh**__

 __
 
• Himachal Pradesh is known for its **terrace farming** and horticulture, especially for producing **apples, plums, and pears**.
 
• The practice of 'slash and burn' agriculture is not commonly associated with this state.
 
 
 
• **Andhra Pradesh**__
 __
 
• Andhra Pradesh primarily practices **irrigated agriculture** due to the presence of rivers like the **Godavari and Krishna**.
 
• 'Slash and burn' agriculture is not a traditional practice in this region.
 
 
 
• **Arunachal Pradesh**__
 
 
• In Arunachal Pradesh, the 'slash and burn' method is commonly referred to as **'Jhum' cultivation**.
 
• This method is widely practiced by the tribal communities in the northeastern states of India.
